name: Glass UI flow
looks: Over a radial colour field with a fine dot grid, three frosted glass cards spring up into a stack, each slightly rotated on arrival before settling square. A cursor flies in, presses a control, flips a toggle, picks an option, and a button turns into a progress fill that counts to completion and becomes a toast notification, before the scene leaves on a soft circle wipe.
build: Build the cards as DOM with a backdrop blur, a translucent fill, a hairline border and a tinted shadow, carried on spring eases (response about 0.36-0.42, damping 0.78-0.85). Drive the cursor on power3 in-out paths with a short press-and-release, and set the progress percentage as text from the clock, using only fictional sample product names.
sound: Blips on each card landing, a click on the press, a toggle tick, a rising tone under the progress, and a chime on completion.
prompt: Show a small interface coming to life: frosted glass cards spring into a stack, a cursor presses a control and flips a toggle, and a button fills with progress before completing and surfacing a confirmation. Use invented sample product names and controls, never a real brand's interface, and let the whole sequence demonstrate how effortless the product is to use.
source: the 2026 Opus showreels; built in examples/reel-2026-10-06.html, S7.
